TypeTogether aimed for a natural feel that noticeably reduces the strict, systematised look of typography, avoiding excessive optical corrections and keeping looser word spacing, as in handwriting.

story.text: Shantell Martin wanted to empower people to read and write, whatever their relationship to words. She is dyslexic, and since childhood had liked how playful and easy to read Comic Sans was.

Martin wrote pangrams with a favourite felt-tip marker, a Staedtler Lumocolor M, and scanned them; the letters were traced from a centred line through the pen strokes, then expanded into Light and ExtraBold strokes.
Martin's artwork, handwriting and creative philosophy; she said she wanted to make “a new Comic Sans”.
The a and g use the single-storey forms kids learn in school, to keep it friendly and familiar, and its metrics are set close to common fonts such as Roboto.

story.text: In late 2017 the studio Fullmasters was hired to develop a wayfinding system to help visitors find Sofia's tourist sights and attractions.
Condensed widths were needed for the different sizes of the two totems and the signboards; the plan grew into a type system with extended language support.

Lettersoup's typeface Attractive, expanded because a modest budget and short deadline ruled out a new family from scratch. The design draws on early-20th-century technical sans serifs, with confident letterforms, a pronounced vertical impetus and tense curves.
The team settled on a straight-sided sans, with narrow proportions and a generous x-height, as a space-saving workhorse for very diverse environments.
The Chief Architect of Sofia Municipality envisioned it as the de facto official typeface of the Bulgarian capital, and Vision for Sofia uses it as its corporate typeface.
